A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-alignment benchmarking and GAPE work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph-alignment experiments, molecular regression comparisons, noise-transfer analyses and positional-encoding experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds reconstruction experiments, architecture comparisons, depth ablations and downstream-correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The central Siamese alignment and GAPE procedures remain. Algorithm 1 corrects the BFS trimming condition from <= N' to > N', and Section 6.3 adds an auxiliary frozen GAPE encoder with a trainable Transformer reconstruction decoder. These are localized procedural changes; the PDFs do not establish that the BFS implementation or original experiments changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds adjacency-matrix reconstruction on ZINC and PCQM4Mv2, including transfer from encoders pretrained on molecular and citation graphs. This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements beyond alignment and molecular regression. The underlying dataset families are retained; ZINC already appeared in v1's regression and pretraining experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPSE. Alignment comparisons add GraphGPS, PNA, SGC, GSN and PPGN, while reconstruction introduces a random baseline. The separate PCQM4Mv2 leaderboard comparison against Graphormer, GPS-Medium, Uni-Mol+, EGT-Large and TGT-At is removed. These changes materially alter comparator membership within the relevant experiments.

E3.justification: New protocols include frozen-encoder reconstruction evaluated by edge accuracy and F1, approximately 60k/140k-parameter architecture comparisons with four/eight layers, and a two-to-seven-layer depth sweep. The larger Transformer leaderboard experiment is removed. Existing alignment splits, noise grids and retained molecular-regression settings remain unchanged; the additions do not establish reruns of those experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds a depth/denoising ablation (Table C.3), capacity and expressivity analyses (Appendices G-H), alignment-to-downstream correlations (Appendix I), and reconstruction threshold sensitivity against a random baseline (Appendix M). The earlier noise-transfer and pretraining-source analyses remain in Appendix K rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Pearson-correlation estimation and explicitly specifies four different random seeds for the new depth and extended-architecture studies. Existing ten-run alignment and four-run positional-encoding reporting remain unchanged. The removed leaderboard experiment's two-run averages disappear; this is not evidence of reduced replication for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained alignment, transfer and edge-feature tables are numerically unchanged. Added GPSE changes the best reported ZINC mean in Table 1 to 0.104 ± 0.006, versus GAPE+RWPE's retained 0.109 ± 0.005. Reconstruction adds 97.7-98.8% accuracy and 94.0-94.7% F1, alongside new depth, architecture and correlation results. V1's leaderboard GAPE MAEs of 0.0497, 0.0441 and 0.0337 are removed.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained equivariance theorem A.1, v2 adds an automorphism-invariant-loss theorem and proof (B.2), a graph-distance derivation (C.2.2), and node-equivalence accuracy/loss bounds with a WL-hierarchy corollary (C.3). It also introduces a cited Erdős-Rényi recovery condition and formal isotropic/anisotropic definitions. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the PCQM4Mv2 state-of-the-art and parameter-efficiency contribution emphasized throughout v1. It instead claims graph alignment generalizes the WL test and learns a high-fidelity compression of graph structure, supported by approximately 98% reconstruction accuracy. The abstract, contributions and conclusion therefore redefine a substantial part of the paper's claimed achievement.

C2.justification: V2 adds metric-learning and denoising interpretations, a structural-bottleneck interpretation of downstream correlations, and compression/transferability interpretations of reconstruction. It explicitly discusses potentially nonoptimal planted alignments on small or highly corrupted graphs and the absence of general recovery guarantees beyond Erdős-Rényi graphs. It also attributes GPSE's ZINC advantage to cycle-count pretraining and removes the earlier edge-feature limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a direct repository link, extended-model hyperparameters in Table G.7, and separate pretraining/downstream runtimes in Table L.14. The multi-GPU training details for the removed leaderboard study disappear. Most existing implementation, optimizer, hardware and data-split disclosures are retained; the new link does not establish a newly released resource.

R1.justification: Appendix C.2 substantially expands comparison with prior combinatorial benchmarks, including counting, biconnectivity and coloring tasks. New positioning connects alignment to metric learning, denoising, BYOL and WL expressivity, with additional references supporting these discussions and GPSE/higher-order comparisons. The previous leaderboard-specific positioning and associated references are reduced.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, contributions and conclusion, reframes Section 6 around structural representations, and replaces its leaderboard subsection with reconstruction. It swaps the conclusion and limitations, reorganizes the appendices, removes the NeurIPS checklist, and adds impact and acknowledgement sections. These changes materially reshape the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout with running headers. V2 adds numerous analytical and experimental tables plus correlation and reconstruction-F1 figures, expands Table 1, and replaces the leaderboard Table 2 with reconstruction results. Retained diagrams, benchmark tables and noise-transfer plots are resized or relocated rather than constituting new evidence.

improvement.justification: Broader architecture comparisons, a depth ablation, downstream correlations, and frozen-encoder reconstruction with a random control substantially strengthen evidence that alignment measures useful structural representations. Symmetry analysis, noise-validity caveats and clearer resource access also improve assessability. These gains outweigh losing the separate leaderboard study, although reconstruction protocols and uncertainty remain underdocumented, and Appendix I overstates its correlations: Figure I.1 includes -0.896 despite claiming all are below -0.90.
